rows.note: Use this when the mien specifically means a facial expression rather than a person's general bearing or attitude.

example.english: When they heard the news, their mien immediately became very serious.
example.traditional: 佢一聽到個消息，表情即刻變得好凝重。
example.jyutping: keoi5 jat1 teng1 dou3 go3 siu1 sik1 biu2 cing4 zik1 hak1 bin3 dak1 hou2 jing4 zung6

rows.note: Use this when the mien refers specifically to the person's attitude or manner toward something.

example.english: Their mien toward the new colleague is really uncomfortable to witness.
example.traditional: 佢對住新同事嗰種態度，真係令人好唔舒服。
example.jyutping: keoi5 deoi3 zyu6 san1 tung4 si6 go2 zung2 taai3 dou6 zan1 hai6 ling6 jan4 hou2 m4 syu1 fuk6

rows.note: This is the colloquial all-purpose choice for someone's outward look or general bearing when no narrower meaning is intended.

example.english: Your cheerful mien today makes me wonder if something good happened.
example.traditional: 你今日個樣咁精神，係咪有咩開心事呀？
example.jyutping: nei5 gam1 jat6 go3 joeng6 gam3 zing1 san4 hai6 mai6 jau5 me1 hoi1 sam1 si6 aa3
